transcription.note: The core CASH+ model of C-S-H in the Ca-Si-H2O system. Its formula unit has four sites: DU, a fixed dreierketten unit T = Ca2Si2O5(OH)2; BT, the bridging tetrahedron, holding a silicate S = SiO2OH-, a vacancy v = OH- or a calcium C = CaOOH-; IC, the interlayer cation, holding a vacancy v = H+ or a calcium C = CaH(OH)2+; IW, a fixed interlayer water h = H2O. Each site has coefficient 1, and each end-member puts one moiety on each site, so the six end-members are named T, the BT moiety, the IC moiety and h. The G and H of the end-members are those of Table 8, final step 5; their S and Cp are the VBT estimates of Table 4, their V the volumes of Table 4 (from the densities of Section 3.4).

cashplus_end_members.location: Table 10 (p. 14), bulk formulas; Table 2 gives the same compositions as moieties

cashplus_standard_properties.location: G and H: Table 8 (final step 5), p. 11; S, Cp (VBT estimates) and V: Table 4, p. 6; density: Section 3.4, p. 10

cashplus_interactions.location: Table 8 (final step 5), p. 11; the symmetric Berman site-interaction model of Section 2.6 and Appendix A1, Eqs. (13)-(17)

CaSiO3_aq_G.description: Standard Gibbs energy of formation of the aqueous complex CaSiO3@ at 25 C, refitted with the core model (log K = 4.0 for Ca+2 + SiO3-2 = CaSiO3@).

CaSiO3_aq_H.description: Standard enthalpy of formation of CaSiO3@ at 25 C.

CaSiO3_aq_S.description: Standard entropy of CaSiO3@ at 25 C, constrained on the C-S-H solubility at 50 and 85-90 C.

CaSiO3_aq_Cp.description: Standard heat capacity of CaSiO3@ at 25 C, taken as constant.

silica_saturation_Ca_Si.description: Bulk Ca/Si below which amorphous silica is stable beside C-S-H in the Ca-Si-H2O system at 25 C.

portlandite_saturation_Ca_Si.location: Section 3.3, p. 10 ('Above C/S = 1.64'); the fit constrained the Ca/Si of C-S-H beside portlandite close to 1.65 (p. 9)
portlandite_saturation_Ca_Si.description: Ca/Si of C-S-H at portlandite saturation in the Ca-Si-H2O system at 25 C.

edh_ion_size.description: Common ion-size parameter of the extended Debye-Hueckel equation used for the fit, in Angstrom (KOH as major electrolyte).

edh_b_gamma.description: Extended-term parameter b_gamma of the extended Debye-Hueckel equation used for the fit (KOH as major electrolyte).

CaSiO3_aq_dH_reaction.description: Standard enthalpy of the reaction Ca+2 + SiO3-2 = CaSiO3@ at 25 C.

CaSiO3_aq_dS_reaction.description: Standard entropy of the reaction Ca+2 + SiO3-2 = CaSiO3@ at 25 C.

CaSiO3_aq_dCp_reaction.description: Standard heat capacity of the reaction Ca+2 + SiO3-2 = CaSiO3@, taken as constant.

notes: Table 10 repeats the end-member data with its G and H columns out of step with the rows: the G printed on the TSvh row (-5347.54) is the G of TCCh in Table 8, and so on down the table, and the column header says J/mol where the values are in kJ/mol. The formulas and volumes of Table 10 are in step with its rows; the G and H transcribed here are those of Table 8, the table the footnote of Table 10 names as their source.

With the element entropies of CODATA, G = H - T (S - sum of the element entropies) holds to 0.01 kJ/mol for five end-members and for CaSiO3@. It holds to 0.28 kJ/mol for TSvh, whose printed H (-5032.03) would give it exactly as -5032.31: the printed H is most probably a transposition of digits. The printed values are kept; G is the fitted quantity and is what fixes the equilibria at 25 C.
The G of CaSiO3@ is 3.42 kJ/mol above that of Cemdata18 (-1517.5569 kJ/mol): the core model is fitted together with this value, and a database running the model carries it.
Portlandite and amorphous silica are those of PSI-Nagra 12/07 and Cemdata18 (Table 10, footnote); both databases give them the same G at 25 C.
The site fractions at portlandite saturation are printed as rounded percentages.
